title: Average salary in Argentina 2026 (in USD, by role)
summary: The average salary in Argentina for a skilled professional runs 800 to 1,500 dollars a month. What that means in pesos, what it costs to hire, and why it moves.
body_markdown:
The average salary in Argentina for a skilled professional is commonly **800 to 1,500 US dollars a month** in Buenos Aires, with senior and specialised roles above that range. The figure in pesos and the figure in dollars tell different stories, and the dollar figure is the one that survives the quarter.


This guide covers what the average salary in Argentina actually is in 2026, how it breaks down by role, what it costs a company to hire there, and why the currency question matters more here than anywhere else in the region.


## Key takeaways


- Skilled professionals in Buenos Aires commonly earn 800 to 1,500 dollars a month, with senior engineering above it.
- Argentine salaries converted to dollars are among the lowest in the region for comparable seniority.
- Inflation means a salary agreed in pesos loses value between the agreement and the payday.
- Paying in dollars has become standard practice for technical talent working with foreign companies.
- Cross-border payouts lose 3 to 7 percent to fees and FX before they arrive (McKinsey Global Payments Report, 2026), so the offer and the deposit are different numbers.


## What is the average salary in Argentina in 2026?


### The dollar figure


For skilled professionals in Buenos Aires the common range is 800 to 1,500 dollars a month. Argentina sits in the upper half of Latin American professional pay in local terms and near the bottom in dollar terms, which is the whole tension of hiring there: the talent is expensive locally and inexpensive internationally.


For context across the region, the regional minimum wage averaged about 400 dollars a month at the start of 2026 (Statista, 2026), and professional pay across major Latin American cities commonly runs 600 to 2,000 dollars a month. The full regional picture is in[average salary in Latin America](https://www.getontop.com/blog/the-average-salary-in-peru-argentina-mexico-colombia-and-brazil) .


### Why the peso number and the dollar number disagree


A salary quoted in pesos is a moving target. Between the month it is agreed and the month it is spent, inflation removes part of it, and the exchange rate used to convert it decides how much. Two people on the same nominal peso salary can end up with materially different purchasing power depending only on when they converted.


That is why job listings, offers, and benchmark reports for Argentine technical roles are increasingly quoted in dollars. It is not a preference. It is the only way to state a number that still means the same thing in three months.


## Average salary in Argentina by role


Role Common monthly range (USD) Notes


Software engineer Top of the professional range and above Senior and specialised roles compete with foreign employers


Data and analytics Upper half of the range Demand rising faster than local supply


Product and graphic design Middle of the range Portfolio matters more than credentials


Finance and accounting Middle of the range International reporting experience commands a premium


Bilingual customer support Lower half of the range High turnover when pay is not held in USD


Across Latin America, software engineer base pay runs 30,000 to 63,000 dollars a year, 50 to 70 percent below US levels (Near, 2026). Argentina sits at the lower end of that band in dollar terms while producing engineers who compete for the same remote roles as the rest of the region.


## What it costs a company to hire in Argentina


### Contractor or employee


The salary is not the cost. A contractor costs the agreed rate plus a platform fee. An employee costs the salary plus local employer contributions plus the administrative overhead of running local payroll, and Argentine employment carries strong protections that make the exit as expensive as the entry.


Most foreign companies start with contractors and move long-term roles to an employer of record. The trap is deciding the model on paperwork rather than on the substance of the work, which is covered in[outsourcing to Argentina](https://www.getontop.com/blog/outsourcing-argentina-benefits-challenges) .


### Price the role, not the country


Country averages are a starting point and a poor budget. The[contractor cost by country calculator](https://www.getontop.com/calculator/contractor-cost-by-country) gives current rates for Argentina by role, and the[employee cost calculator](https://www.getontop.com/calculator/employee-cost) adds the employer contributions a contractor rate does not include.


## Paying an Argentine salary so it keeps its value


### Dollars or pesos


In a high inflation market the payout currency is not an administrative preference, it is most of the compensation. A raise agreed in pesos can be gone within a quarter. The same amount delivered in dollars holds, and the worker decides when to convert.


Workers paid into an[Ontop Global Account](https://www.getontop.com/ontop-global-account) receive and hold their income in USD, spend from it with a card, and convert on their own schedule. That moves the currency risk to the person best placed to time it, and it removes the quarterly renegotiation that peso salaries produce.


### What you send is not what lands


Cross-border payouts lose 3 to 7 percent to fees and FX before arriving (McKinsey Global Payments Report, 2026). Two companies can offer the same salary, and the one that pays cleanly effectively pays more. The mechanics of the rate decision are in[multi-currency payroll](https://www.getontop.com/blog/managing-multiple-currencies-international-payroll-strategies) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the average salary in Argentina in US dollars?


For skilled professionals in Buenos Aires, commonly 800 to 1,500 dollars a month, with senior engineering and specialised roles above that. Outside Buenos Aires the range is lower.


### What is the average monthly salary in Argentina?


Professional pay commonly falls between 800 and 1,500 dollars a month. The regional minimum wage across Latin America averaged about 400 dollars a month at the start of 2026 (Statista, 2026).


### Is the average wage in Argentina higher than in the rest of Latin America?


In local purchasing terms Argentina sits in the upper half of the region. Converted to dollars it sits near the bottom for comparable seniority, which is why it is attractive to foreign employers and frustrating for local workers at the same time.


### Why do Argentine salaries change so fast?


Inflation and exchange rate movement. A figure quoted in pesos can describe a different amount of purchasing power within a single quarter, so any benchmark more than a few months old should be treated as directional.


### Can a foreign company pay an Argentine worker in dollars?


Yes, and most do. The practical requirement is that the person can receive and hold dollars in an account they control, rather than having the amount converted on arrival at a rate they did not choose.


### How much does it cost to hire a developer in Argentina?


Less than a comparable US hire by a wide margin, with the exact figure depending on seniority and whether you engage them as a contractor or an employee. Price the specific role rather than the country average.


## What to do next


If you are hiring, price one role both ways, contractor and employee, with contributions and fees included, and decide the payment currency before you make the offer. If you are being hired, ask which currency you will be paid in and which exchange rate applies. Those two questions decide more of your real pay than the headline number does.
